annotations.annotation_text: Structural opening of Book 2, Chapter 3, page 324. Continues the multi-layered dream narrative depicting the nocturnal transmigration of human history and Dublin topography.
sources: Campbell, Joseph and Robinson, Henry Morton. A Skeleton Key to Finnegans Wake. https://archive.org/details/skeletonkeytofin00camp
McHugh, Roland. Annotations to Finnegans Wake. https://jhupbooks.press.jhu.edu/title/annotations-finnegans-wake

annotations.annotation_text: Mid-page polysemic discourse on page 324: Joyce weaves multilingual puns, etymological roots, and rhythmic cadences capturing the shifting consciousness of the collective unconscious.
sources: Tindall, William York. A Reader's Guide to Finnegans Wake. https://archive.org/details/readersguidetofi00tind
Atherton, James S. The Books at the Wake. https://archive.org/details/booksatwake0000athe

annotations.annotation_text: Dublin geographical anchor (Clontarf): grounding the cosmic oneiric myth in the tangible stone, water, and hills of County Dublin and the River Liffey.
sources: Joyce, P.W. The Origin and History of Irish Names of Places. https://archive.org/details/originandhistory01joycuoft
